name: Buy, blend and deliver chemicals
summary: Each frac pad needs friction reducer, surfactants, biocide and other additives mixed into the water, mostly in blends the company makes at its own plant. A buyer nets each pad's chemical requirement against stock and orders raw additives from suppliers, plant operators blend, test and package the product, and warehouse staff prepare dangerous goods paperwork and send the totes to the pad, where the blender operator receives them. Long supplier lead times (worst after the February 2021 Gulf Coast freeze), late design changes and a single blending plant make shortages and urgent hot-shot deliveries a regular event.

baseline.org_archetype: A TSX-listed Canadian pressure pumper with about 1,350 employees, six to eight 24-hour frac crews, a 70-person supply chain department in Calgary and at district bases, an ERP with procurement and inventory, and spreadsheets, email and phone for day-to-day logistics.
baseline.notes: One chemical blending and packaging plant in the Calgary or Red Deer area with eight operators on extended hours.

unit_of_work: one chemical order (the additives for one pad, or a base stock top-up)
trigger: A frac program issues a chemical requirement for a pad, or a district base asks to top up stock.
end_state: The blended chemicals are on location or at the base, signed for and moved to the job in the ERP.

volume.seasonality: Follows frac activity: highest January to mid-March, lowest in spring break-up.

evidence.note: About 50 wells a month (organisation file) on 15-20 pads, with a few orders per pad for initial supply and top-ups, plus base stock orders.

surge.cause: Winter completion and drilling peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Same winter peak as the proppant and frac processes in the organisation file; the organisation file entry for this process has no surge.
One buyer spends part of their time on chemical orders; author's estimate.
Eight plant operators on extended hours (organisation file); about half their time on frac blends, the rest on cleaning, maintenance and cementing additives. Author's estimate.
Plant warehouse staff for receiving, shipping documents and loading; author's estimate.
Substitute approvals and design revisions. Not listed for this process in the organisation file process map.
Receiving totes on location. Not listed for this process in the organisation file process map.

systems.name: ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
Laboratory test records (lab database and spreadsheets)
Dispatch and crew scheduling board (scheduling module, whiteboards, spreadsheets)
Fracture and cement placement modelling software

resources.name: Crew pickup trucks and light vehicles

steps.name: Receive pad chemical requirement
steps.description: The procurement specialist who buys chemicals opens the chemical requirement from the frac program: litres or kilograms of each additive (friction reducer, surfactant, biocide, scale inhibitor, breaker, crosslinker) by pad, the start date and the delivery point. They log it in the chemical demand workbook.

error.defect_description: Loading or volume copied wrongly from the design.

evidence.note: Program design flows into procurement and coordination of chemicals (trican_frac); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check finished and raw stock
steps.description: The buyer checks ERP stock of blended products and raw additives at the blending plant and the district bases, then phones the plant to confirm what is physically on the floor because counts drift. They net the requirement against stock already promised to other pads.

error.defect_description: ERP stock overstated; shortage found at blending.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the organisation file notes inaccurate counts in the warehouse process.

steps.name: Create purchase order for additives
steps.description: The buyer raises a purchase order in the ERP to the contracted chemical supplier for the missing additives, by product code, quantity in totes or drums, and required date, and emails it to the supplier.

error.defect_description: Wrong product grade or package size ordered.

control.basis: Delegation of authority and approved supplier list for chemical purchases

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Supplier confirms order and ship date
steps.description: The chemical supplier's order desk checks its stock and production schedule and confirms quantity and ship date by email, or reports that the product is on allocation or back-ordered.

evidence.note: Petrochemical force majeure and restocking problems through much of 2021 (dallasfed_2021) and chemical inflation and supply disruptions (step_2021). Share is the author's estimate across 2019-2022.

steps.name: Find a substitute or alternative source
steps.description: The buyer calls other suppliers for the same product or an equivalent, gathers technical data sheets and safety data sheets, and proposes a substitute to engineering if the original cannot arrive before the pad starts.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve substitute additive
steps.description: The completions design engineer compares the substitute's chemistry and loading with the fluid design, asks the lab for a compatibility check if needed, and approves it, changes the loading or rejects it.

error.defect_description: Substitute approved without a compatibility test.

control.basis: Fluid system changes need engineering approval and lab compatibility testing

evidence.note: Engineered fluid systems tested in the company lab (trican_frac); this approval step is the author's description.

steps.name: Additives in transit
steps.description: The supplier ships totes, drums or bulk liquid by truck from Alberta distribution warehouses or from US Gulf Coast plants, with customs clearance on cross-border loads.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: one to fourteen days depending on origin.

steps.name: Receive additives at the plant
steps.description: A warehouse attendant unloads the shipment with a forklift, checks product codes and quantities against the purchase order, checks the supplier labels, safety data sheets and certificates of analysis, and posts the goods receipt in the ERP.

error.defect_description: Receipt posted to the wrong lot or location.

control.basis: WHMIS supplier labels and safety data sheets (Hazardous Products Act and Regulations)

next.condition: wrong product, damage or missing paperwork

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Resolve receiving discrepancy
steps.description: The buyer contacts the supplier about the wrong product, damaged totes or missing certificate, arranges a return or replacement, and decides whether the product can be used meanwhile.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Schedule the blend batch
steps.description: The plant operator adds the blend to the plant schedule, slotting it by pad start date against other batches, and pulls the recipe sheet for the product.

error.defect_description: Batch scheduled after the pad needs it.

next.condition: design or loading changed before blending

evidence.note: The company runs one blending plant (organisation file); schedule wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Revise chemical schedule after a design change
steps.description: When the customer or engineer changes the fluid system or loadings, the design engineer issues a revised chemical schedule and blend ratios, and the buyer re-nets the requirement.

error.defect_description: Revision not passed to the plant.

evidence.note: Sudden design changes named in the organisation file; share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Blend and package the batch
steps.description: Two plant operators charge the mixing tank, meter each component by weight or flow meter, mix for the set time and fill totes or drums. They wear chemical PPE and work under the plant's hazard assessment and spill containment rules.

control.basis: Plant hazard assessment, chemical PPE and spill containment (Alberta OHS Code Part 2 and Part 4 chemical hazards)

evidence.note: Batch time and crew size are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Test batch and send QC sample
steps.description: The plant operator measures specific gravity, pH and viscosity on a retained sample, records them on the batch sheet and sends a sample to the lab for a batch performance check.

evidence.note: Chemical batches checked by the company lab (trican_frac, organisation file); tests listed are the author's description.

steps.name: Review lab result and release batch
steps.description: When the lab posts its result, the plant operator compares it with the product specification and releases the batch for shipping, or holds it for adjustment.

control.basis: Product specification: batch released only after a passing QC result

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Label totes and post production
steps.description: The plant operator applies product labels and dangerous goods safety marks to each tote, then posts the production order in the ERP to consume raw additives and add the finished product to stock.

control.basis: TDG Regulations Part 4 safety marks and WHMIS workplace labels

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Book delivery and raise shipment request
steps.description: A warehouse attendant agrees the delivery time with the frac operations coordinator, books a carrier and raises the dangerous goods shipment request listing products, UN numbers and quantities.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare TDG shipping document
steps.description: The attendant completes the shipping document: consignor, date, UN number, shipping name, class and packing group for each product, quantities, number of totes and the 24-hour number. They check the driver's TDG training certificate and that the trailer is placarded.

error.defect_description: Missing or wrong entry on the shipping document.

control.basis: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations Part 3 (sections 3.1, 3.5, 3.7) and Part 6 training

evidence.note: Shipping document content and duties from tdg_part3; minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Load totes onto the truck
steps.description: The attendant loads the totes with a forklift, secures them and confirms the count against the shipping document with the driver.

next.condition: urgent top-up driven by own staff

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Carrier delivers to pad or base
steps.description: The carrier drives the load to the pad or district base, waiting at the lease gate if the site is not ready to receive.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Drive an urgent top-up to the pad
steps.description: When a pad is about to run short because of a design change or faster pumping, a warehouse attendant drives a pickup and trailer with a few totes to the pad, carrying the shipping document, and returns the same day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of a common hot-shot practice.

steps.name: Receive totes on location
steps.description: The blender operator checks the totes against the shipping document, sets them in secondary containment by the chemical unit and signs the delivery receipt.

error.defect_description: Tote count not checked, so a shortage shows up mid-pad.

control.basis: Customer site rules for chemical storage in secondary containment

evidence.note: Blender operators manage chemical totes on location (organisation file); minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Transfer stock to the job location
steps.description: The warehouse attendant enters the signed receipt in the ERP, moving the product from plant stock to the pad's job location so it can be billed, and logs the returnable totes for pick-up.

error.defect_description: Transfer missed, so pad usage cannot be billed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Long lead time or supplier allocation
exceptions.description: An additive cannot arrive before the pad; a substitute is found and approved by engineering.

exceptions.name: Design change before blending
exceptions.description: The fluid system or loadings change; the chemical schedule is revised and stock re-checked.

exceptions.name: Batch fails QC
exceptions.description: Lab result outside specification; the batch is adjusted or re-blended.

exceptions.name: Urgent hot-shot
exceptions.description: A pad about to run short gets totes driven out by company staff.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from chemical requirement to stock transferred to the job
benchmarks.population: Frac chemical orders at a Canadian pressure pumper, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: three to four days when raw additives are on hand, one to three weeks when they must be ordered.

benchmarks.metric: US basic organic chemicals capacity offline after the February 2021 freeze

pain_points.description: Additive lead times stretched after the 2021 Gulf Coast freeze and with 2021-2022 inflation, so buyers spent time finding substitutes and engineers approving them.
Late changes to fluid designs arrive after blending has been scheduled, causing re-netting and urgent deliveries.

evidence.note: Organisation file process description; frequency is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: A single blending plant is a bottleneck in the winter peak, and ERP stock counts that drift from the floor hide shortages until blending day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Dangerous goods paperwork is filled by hand for each load and errors can stop a truck at a roadside check.

evidence.note: Shipping document duties from tdg_part3; error effect from the organisation file dangerous goods process.

sources.title: Hydraulic Fracturing
sources.supports: Service covers engineering design through procurement and coordination of chemicals, proppants, people and equipment; secure supply of proppants; ceramic proppants sourced on request; full suite of friction reducers and a full line of chemical and fluid systems; high-concentration slickwater products to streamline logistics; full-service lab in Calgary.

sources.title: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations (SOR/2001-286), Part 3 Documentation
sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: Section 3.1: consignor prepares and gives the carrier a shipping document before the carrier takes the goods; section 3.5: consignor name and address, date, UN number, shipping name, class, packing group, quantity, number of containers, 24-hour number; section 3.7: driver keeps the shipping document within reach or in the door pocket. Current consolidation; the same Part 3 duties applied in 2019-2022.

sources.title: Texas winter deep freeze broke refining, petrochemical supply chains (J. Thompson, Southwest Economy, Q2 2021)
sources.supports: February 2021 freeze took up to 80% of US basic organic chemicals capacity offline, up to 60% still offline in mid-March; producers outside Texas declared force majeure for lack of intermediate inputs; restocking expected to stay difficult through much of 2021.

sources.title: STEP Energy Services Ltd. Reports Fourth Quarter and Year End 2021 Results
sources.supports: Canadian fracturing: 1,012,000 tonnes of proppant in 2021 (776,000 in 2020), 977 operating days, proppant per stage 54 tonnes (Q4 2021) to 83 tonnes (2021); product and hauling costs rose with company-supplied proppant; costs rose late in 2021 with supply chain disruptions; weather delays in late December 2021 and extreme cold in January 2022; spring break-up restricts equipment moves; US segment cites inflation on chemicals, proppant and spare parts.

assumptions: The company blends most friction reducer and surfactant packages itself and buys some ready-to-use products; ready-to-use orders skip blending in practice but are not modelled separately.
Classifying products and preparing shipping documents also appear in the dangerous goods shipping process; here the document step is included because it sits in the path of every chemical order.
Lab testing itself belongs to the quality testing process; only sampling and the review of the result appear here.
Blending is done by two operators together (people = 2); the plant is held a little longer than the labour time for set-up and clean-up.
All step times, branch shares and waits are the author's estimates except where a source is cited; no published blending cycle time benchmark was found.
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file (wage x 1.35).
